title: Privacy boundary and ops criteria - Helios Health & Finance intro
topics: Hybrid hosting: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
summary: Intro discovery for privacy and ops constraints. Helios is a health-fintech hybrid handling PHI and payment data across EU and US. Primary concerns: where logs live, key residency, audit trails, and ability to run an on-prem or VPC private control plane. AE/SE outlined host/dedicated/private tradeoffs, suggested pilot sandbox and security docs. Agreed next steps for technical deep dive and pilot provisioning.
next_steps: Send SOC2 + HIPAA and SOC 2++ compress whitepaper link (Ethan) by 2027-04-09
Schedule infra deep dive with SREs (Priya) week of 2027-04-18
Provision 2-week Dedicated sandbox with EU region nodes (Noah) with sample dataset - target 2027-04-20
action_items: Ethan Morales: share security + architecture pack and redwood compliance matrix:2027-04-09
Priya Rao: prepare latency & cost estimate for small-payload patient-intake flows:2027-04-15
Mikael Berg: provide example traffic profile and retention requirements to Redwood:2027-04-12
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-08
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood SE), Jesse (Redwood CSM), Ariana (Helios Head of Security), Tomás (Platform Lead), Sophie (Privacy Counsel), Mikael (SRE)

[00:00] Ethan Morales: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros - I'm Ethan, account exec on the inference team at Redwood. Priya and Noah here are our SEs who will handle the technical bits, and Jesse's on CSM.
[00:08] Ariana Vega: Hi, Ariana here. thanks for running this. We're Helios Health & Finance, we do payment processing for clinics and run patient intake forms in EU and US. It has PHI so we need to understand hosting and log flows.
[00:18] Tomás Ruiz: And I'm Tomás, platform lead. quick note: timeline is Q3 pilot and decision by end of Q3. key criteria are data residency, key control, and minimal exposure of logs to third parties.
[00:28] Priya Rao: Great. high level, we want to cover Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options and mapping to your compliance gates — GDPR, HIPAA, audit trails, and key residency/KMS. We'll also flag common gotchas like control plane logs and SaaS metadata.
[00:40] Sophie Nguyen: For privacy counsel perspective: we need evidence that PHI never leaves the EU for EU patient flows, and we need an audit trail for all model invocations retaining who called what, and redaction options for PII in logs.
[00:52] Noah Kim: Noted. Quick clarifying q: when you say 'never leaves EU' do you mean compute, keys, and logs all within EU, or is cross-border allowed if encrypted?
[01:03] Ariana Vega: Prefer everything — compute & keys in region — especially for patient data. We might accept tokenized payloads to hosted instances but need to confirm.
[01:12] Ethan Morales: Understood. to set expectations: Hosted API is fastest but runs in our multi-tenant control plane — we have region pinning for EU and US, but some metadata and control-plane traces may live in central telemetry unless we enable Private.
[01:27] Tomás Ruiz: That's the crux. we can't have a SaaS control plane storing full logs for EU PHI calls. What are options short-term?
[01:36] Priya Rao: Two main routes: Dedicated — reserved capacity in a given region with isolated runtime and no sharing of GPU pools, and Private — a private control plane in your VPC or on-prem where logs and keys are customer-managed. Dedicated reduces cross-tenant exposure but control plane logs may still be in Redwood's control plane unless we enable Private or a logging-forwarding flow.
[01:58] Mikael Berg: can you describe log forwarding? we'd want logs to be pushed to our Splunk in the EU and only store redacted traces in Redwood.
[02:07] Noah Kim: yes — we support syslog/S3 sink options. there's a streaming forwarding feature that can push raw logs to your endpoint; we can also redact fields server-side before forwarding but redact rules are best-effort and sometimes require schema alignment. sometimes the transcriber showed 'K-V cash' instead of 'KV cache'— apologies for the audio glitch earlier.
[02:30] Sophie Nguyen: important: forwarding is fine only if the logs never persist in Redwood's longer-term store in the clear. we need to know retention windows and whether the logs are encrypted at rest with customer managed keys.
[02:44] Jesse Alvarez: for Dedicated and Private we can support customer KMS integration. on Private, you manage the KMS and HSM; on Dedicated we support BYOK where keys can be in your KMS but there are nuances — e.g. control plane backups may still be encrypted with Redwood-managed keys unless you opt for Private with full key control.
[03:05] Ariana Vega: how confident are you about evidence — like certs/attestations — that keys don't leave EU or that logs are physically stored in EU?
[03:14] Ethan Morales: we have SOC 2 Type II, and we maintain auditors' attestations. For region-specific proof, we can provide architecture diagrams and data flow maps showing regional tenancy; for Private we can deliver evidence that no Redwood-managed artifacts remain. We'll attach the SOC2/HIPAA pack after call.
[03:30] Tomás Ruiz: let's talk about HIPAA: any PHI in prompts — are we responsible for BAA?
[03:36] Priya Rao: Redwood signs BAAs for customers handling PHI. we do have HIPAA controls across hosting and we can do dedicated deployments with a BAA attached; for strict PHI residency we recommend Private so you run the control plane and key management.
[03:50] [04:00] Ariana Vega: curious about telemetry — what telemetry is unavoidable in Hosted? IPs? caller metadata? how granular?
[04:08] Noah Kim: some metadata for billing/usage is retained such as request counters and anonymized usage math. In Hosted you can't guarantee zero metadata; Dedicated reduces that, but again control plane events - like scaling decisions - hit our central telemetry.
[04:25] Sophie Nguyen: we need to quantify retention — can you give typical retention windows for request logs, debug traces, and aggregated metrics?
[04:33] Priya Rao: default retention: request logs 30 days, debug traces 90 days, metrics 13 months. for enterprise Dedicated we can adjust retention or disable request log retention and forward immediately to customer S3 with 0-day retention in Redwood.
[04:50] Mikael Berg: about PII redaction — is it deterministic? for example SSNs or patient names in free-text prompts — can we auto-redact before persistent storage?
[04:59] Noah Kim: we have configurable pre-send hooks and masking rules. redaction uses regex and token detectors; for PHI we recommend client-side tokenization and server-side redaction as defense-in-depth. sometimes ASR or NLP-derived detectors miss obfuscated PHI so we advise more conservative retention policies.
[05:18] Tomás Ruiz: can you run through an example flow: patient submits intake in EU -> inference model generates suggestions -> logs and KV cache — where do they land in Dedicated vs Private?
[05:29] Priya Rao: Dedicated: compute runs in EU region with isolated GPU pool. request bodies can be configured to be forwarded to your S3 (EU) and Redwood's short-term store for operational replay can be disabled. KV cache lives on the runtime node — we can encrypt with customer key. Private: both runtime and control plane run in your VPC, logs and metrics go to your endpoints, and you retain full key control and audit.
[05:52] Ariana Vega: so for Pilot we likely need Dedicated EU with immediate forwarding and zero-retention in Redwood. is that feasible?
[06:00] Ethan Morales: yes feasible as a pilot. we'll provision a Dedicated sandbox in eu-west-1, enable S3 forwarding to your EU account, set request log retention to 0, and provide docs. there are caveats like operational traces retained briefly for incident investigation but we can require a retention SLA and mutual process for purging.
[06:21] Sophie Nguyen: who has the final purge authority? if an incident occurs, can Redwood retain minimal traces for forensics? we need contract language.
[06:29] Jesse Alvarez: we can add clauses to limit retention and require explicit approval to retain forensics longer than X days; for Private deployments you control everything. for Dedicated we propose a jointly agreed runbook.
[06:44] [06:50] Tomás Ruiz: on keys: BYOK sounds attractive. is the latency impact significant when using customer KMS in a remote region?
[06:58] Priya Rao: the first handshake for decrypting model weights or session keys adds a small one-time latency; token-level encryption/decryption on every request is optional — we typically wrap long-lived runtime keys with the customer KMS. worst-case tail latency maybe +20-50ms depending on KMS region. we'll include numbers in the estimate.
[07:18] Mikael Berg: any specific certifications for HSM? we need FIPS 140-2 or 140-3 compliance and HSM-backed keys for EU residency.
[07:27] Noah Kim: yes, we support integrations with FIPS-compliant HSM providers and can document that for Private deployments.
[07:33] Ariana Vega: threat model question: who can access raw prompts? SREs? support? how are access controls audited?
[07:40] Priya Rao: access is RBAC gated, audited via our audit logs. for Dedicated we restrict access to on-call ops with just-in-time access and you can require approvals for any access. for Private, you can control access fully in your environment.
[07:55] Sophie Nguyen: audit logs must show user, action, timestamp, and purpose. retention policy again — we need to mirror our internal 7-year retention for some records — is that compatible?
[08:05] Ethan Morales: metrics-wise yes, but storing that long with Redwood might be unusual; we can push logs to your archive S3 and you keep it for 7 years. Redwood's own retention wouldn't need to be 7 years if you take ownership.
[08:17] Tomás Ruiz: what about data subject access requests (DSAR) under GDPR — if a patient requests deletion, can we purge all traces quickly?
[08:25] Noah Kim: DSAR deletion requires coordination: if logs are forwarded to your S3, you can delete. if there's Redwood retention, we can run targeted purge based on request IDs within the contractual SLA. for Private, it's straightforward.
[08:38] [08:45] Ariana Vega: any legal exposures if a third-party model has memorized PHI? we use Redwood-hosted open models.
[08:52] Priya Rao: model training data concerns are valid — Redwood verifies model provenance for cataloged models; we also offer model governance: pinning to vetted model versions and avoiding models with problematic data sources. for highest risk, we can host private model weights in your env (Private).
[09:10] Sophie Nguyen: can Redwood provide an architecture diagram that explicitly marks EU data flows and shows where control-plane metadata might cross borders?
[09:18] Ethan Morales: yes we'll share that.
[09:20] Tomás Ruiz: on SLA — we need guaranteed latency p95 and availability. Dedicated SLAs?
[09:27] Jesse Alvarez: Dedicated includes throughput/latency targets with credits for breach and can be scoped in contract. Private availability depends on your infra. We'll propose SLA targets in the proposal.
[09:38] Mikael Berg: do you support offline deploy — like fully airgapped on-prem?
[09:43] Noah Kim: we offer on-prem Private deployments with an appliance-like package for air-gapped installs. that path has longer lead times and additional ops work.
[09:52] [10:00] Ariana Vega: want to circle back to logs: what fields are considered PII/PHI by Redwood and can you provide sample redaction profiles?
[10:08] Priya Rao: we'll share redaction profiles. typically request body, prompt_text, user_identifiers are considered sensitive. we can mask or hash IDs prior to storage.
[10:17] Sophie Nguyen: we'll share a sample redaction policy and expected compliance language.
[10:21] Ethan Morales: quick ops question for Mikael — can you describe expected throughput, average tokens per request, and concurrency? helps us size pilot.
[10:30] Mikael Berg: average 3 requests/sec per service with spikes up to 40 concurrent during morning intake windows; typical payloads are small — 200 tokens.
[10:40] Priya Rao: perfect. we'll run a cost/latency estimate for that profile.
[10:46] [11:00] Tomás Ruiz: one more: are there any places Redwood keeps derived features or embeddings that we should worry about?
[11:06] Noah Kim: embeddings can be configured to not be retained or to be forwarded to your own vector DB in EU. by default Hosted stores embeddings for indexing, but Dedicated/Private gives control.
[11:18] Sophie Nguyen: okay. good.
[11:20] Ethan Morales: recapping: Helios wants a Q3 pilot; short-term path is Dedicated EU sandbox with immediate S3 forwarding and 0-day Redwood retention, BYOK for runtime keys, and redaction rules. next steps: we'll send security pack and architecture, Priya/Noah will prepare latency/cost and we'll schedule an infra deep dive.
[11:40] Ariana Vega: thanks. we'll review and route to procurement.
[11:45] Jesse Alvarez: I'll send draft NDA/BAA templates and the proposed pilot statement of work.
[11:52] Tomás Ruiz: thanks all.

End transcript.
